question: Put one pathogen genome in. What does each stage of the onset arm hand the next, does any stage cover less than the stage before it, and what changes when the reference changes?
answer: Five stages run, and the record carries the input and output of each, under both references. The surface stage is the one that used to cover less than its input: it had no caller, so the only surfaces ever measured were six named by hand, and SARS-CoV-2's RNA-directed RNA polymerase -- fifth of the ranked candidates -- was never asked about. It is exhaustive here, one row per chain, measured or refused with the reason. Two breaks remain and are recorded rather than drawn over: the library definition reads nothing the surface stage measured, and under a holdout the folding stage cannot cut a mature chain out of the genome because the only boundaries it has are the relative's.

limitations: Stage 5 reads nothing from stages 1 to 4. The library definition is the same whatever the surface stage found, and the arrow a flowchart would draw there does not exist yet.

The gate in stage 3 is advisory: the patch spread across structures of one domain is comparable to the footprint it is thresholded against, so most rows that are not refused on localisation read borderline rather than yes or no.

The gate has a lower bound on patch area and no upper one, so a surface far larger than one footprint passes the area test although it is a region rather than a site. Nothing here turns on it, because every oversized patch in this record is refused on localisation first.

Stage 4 refuses a chain whose annotated range does not transfer rather than aligning it. An alignment would recover the window, and `intake` already carries the aligner; until it is wired, a holdout costs this stage most of its input.
One genome. The chain has been run on four pathogens and this record is one of them, chosen because it is the genome the project leads with.
interpretation: A record of what each stage produced. No binding, affinity, inhibition or antiviral property is predicted for any protein or any library member.
